item.title: Building Effective Agents — Anthropic
item.description:
• Source: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents
  • Author: Erik S. and Barry Zhang (Anthropic)
  • Site: Anthropic Engineering
  • Originally published: 2024-12-19
  • Date added: 2026-10-22

Summary

Anthropic's widely shared engineering post (Dec 2024, by Erik S. and Barry Zhang) argues that the most successful LLM agents are built from simple, composable patterns rather than heavy frameworks. It distinguishes workflows (predefined code paths) from agents (models directing their own tool use), recommends starting with a single optimized LLM call and adding complexity only when it measurably helps, and walks through the augmented LLM plus five workflow patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer, before covering autonomous agents. Appendices cover where agents work well today (customer support, coding) and how to "prompt engineer" tools: easy formats, clear docs, and poka-yoke design. Note: the page says much of the tooling landscape has changed since it was written.

Scott's Reads: an AI-narrated summary of the source above. Listen to the episode, then read the original.
